thread:
maria.g: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector rollout we see ~12% P50 CPU increase on host-preparse for short requests (<32 tokens). Hits look concentrated in tokenization + grpc smallwrite. @cheng.w @kevin any ideas?
cheng.w: Ugh. Can you share a flamegraph or perf output? My first guess is the selector pushed short-paths off the fast SIMD kernel.
maria.g: Pasted minimal trace from the canary box:
```
perf record -F 99 -a -g -- ./microbench --short-requests 10000
perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
```
Summary numbers from the run: tokenization 28ms -> 38ms avg, grpc writev smallwrite count +40%, decode CPU unchanged. KV cache miss rate +4% on short seqs.
perf-bot: deploy-bot: rolled kernel-selector v3 -> v2 on canary (host-preparse-canary) at 3829991020 :white_check_mark:
kevin: KV-shard alignment change tracks with that kernel path switch — new kernel alters prefetch stride so hot shard range changed, causing kv miss bump. Short requests over-index smallwrite path so grpc writev overhead amplifies. Suggest: pin short-seq requests to previous kernel, revert batching min_size for shortseqs to 8, and re-run microbench.
jen_ops: On it — will pin kernel for seq_len<=32 on canary and kick off the microbench + telemetry capture. Also adding a metric for smallwrite writev count and per-request kv-miss-rate to make the regression obvious in dashboards.
cheng.w: If pin fixes, follow-up is to implement adaptive kernel selection: prefer fast-mini-kernel for seq_len<=64 and fallback otherwise. Also tweak batching heuristics to favor lower latency for tiny requests (decrease min_batch_size, increase batch timeout for short path).
maria.g: Thanks — canary pinned, telemetry shows tail back to baseline after pin. I'll open an RFC for adaptive selector + batching rule changes and add the KV-shard alignment test to CI microbench. :thumbsup:
